target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for post-transplant relapse
comment: HCT2 is the necessary backbone and I ranked its enabler high too, so no quarrel with it as the platform. My problem is what got left off: pmid:23918951 shows roughly half relapse again even after a second-transplant CR, and this TP53-aberrant complex-karyotype disease already slipped GVL once, so a backbone-only plan banks on deliverability and leaves the cure ceiling untouched. Parking the entire HA-1/WT1 axis, the explicit reason this case was submitted, means zero ranked slots for the one lever that could push past the 37% curve.

I'm targeting the critic's rank-5, not the Iomab-B rank-1 I mostly share, because burying HA-1 TCR-T at the bottom purely on evidence maturity under-weights the ceiling in a curative-intent case built around this exact axis. pmid:38683966 is small at n=9, but 4/9 CR with one remission past two years and zero DLTs is a live cure signal, not a footnote. 'Feasibility, not efficacy' is the right RoB label and the wrong ranking when the alternative on offer is more of the chemo backbone she already failed.

Targeting concensusite's rank-5: they put the single highest-tier option in the whole dossier dead last because NCCN/ELN haven't blessed CD45 RIT yet, which is guideline lag doing the driving. pmid:39298738 is a randomized phase 3 with durable CR 17.1% vs 0% (p<0.0001) and EFS HR 0.23 that maps straight onto an 85%-blast marrow headed for transplant. Parking the best-evidenced lever for the actual problem at rank 5 on adoption status optimizes for the wrong variable.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after second allo-HCT (Bleakley platform; TSC-100/TSC-101)
comment: Same rank-1 as me, so this is agreement with a caveat, not a fight. The advocate frames eligibility as fast and cheap to de-risk, but the load-bearing gate isn't retrieving the HLA type, it's the recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor-negative mismatch, a biological coin-flip that genotyping can simply close. If it closes, the next HLA-restricted lever on their slate is WT1 (pmid:31235963), which is relapse-prevention evidence rather than active-relapse salvage, so the high-ceiling fallback bench is thinner than the ranking implies.

Ranking a donor TCR-T at n=9, 4/9 CR, above an established transplant platform reads as effect-size chasing to me: the Blood 2024 full text has no per-grade AE table I could retrieve, so 'no DLTs' across 9 patients is the only safety datum on file. In a patient whose ECOG, cardiac and organ function are all undocumented, an uncharacterized-toxicity phase-1 cell product is exactly the pick I hold back. It is also post-HCT2 consolidation by design, so it answers nothing for the 85%-blast marrow in front of us.

I flag rank 4 rather than the rank-1 pick because this is where transplant-timing toxicity actually bites: the veno-occlusive disease that surfaced as a dose-limiting toxicity (2/68), plus a 1% treatment-related death against a modest 21% ORR, is the wrong hepatic risk to carry into a planned HCT2. Gemtuzumab fills the same CD33/CD123-adjacent bridging role with more than 20 years of VOD-monitoring algorithm behind it. On peri-transplant hepatic risk I would sequence the on-label handle ahead of this ADC until organ-function data land.

On the evidence I agree this is the strongest row, and the number I weight most is the grade >=3 treatment-related AE parity, 59.7% vs 59.2%, which says the targeted conditioning did not stack toxicity on top of conventional care. Where I hold back is narrow but load-bearing: SIERRA conditioned first-transplant patients, and choosing conditioning intensity for an HCT2 in someone with no cardiac or organ-function workup is the unverified safety step. Endorse the tolerability signal; the go/no-go stays contingent on a fitness assessment.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
comment: We rank this first for the same reason, so my caveat is specific: the ELN/NCCN endorsement of HCT2 is explicitly conditioned on fitness, and non-relapse mortality in a second allograft is substantial and not broken out in the Christopeit registry abstract. With no ECOG, cardiac or organ-function data on file, she has not yet been shown to sit inside the fit population the guideline is describing. Guideline-consistent, but the fitness gate is still open and the NRM number is unquantified for her.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after second allo-HCT (Bleakley platform; TSC-100/TSC-101, ALLOHA)
comment: The preference fit is real, but a 0.75 efficacy weight in a patient whose own file flags undocumented fitness is not a licence to rank a phase-1 cell product with no retrievable per-grade AE table first. 'No DLTs' across 9 patients is a feasibility statement, not a characterized toxicity profile, and this is consolidation delivered on the back of HCT2 rather than anything that touches the current 85%-blast marrow. Keep it on the board, but behind getting her safely to the transplant it depends on.

This is the pick that worries me most on safety: a dual CD33/CD123 CAR-T means CRS plus on-target myeloablation of normal CD33- and CD123-positive progenitors, and the whole case is xenograft-only with zero post-allo-HCT human data. In a re-transplant candidate that stacks cytokine toxicity and marrow-aplasia risk with no clinical toxicity table to plan against. Xenograft survival curves do not tell me how to manage the patient, so I cannot place it on a ranked slate yet.

Chasing the highest ceiling is the risktaker's job, but PMID 38683966 is n=9, single-arm, 4 of 9 CR with no comparator and a feasibility endpoint, ROBINS-I Serious, and the per-term AE table is not even retrievable. A 4/9 uncontrolled response fraction is a signal to run the next trial on, not grounds to rank this above the one randomized phase 3 in the file. The double gate (HLA-A*02:01 plus a recipient HA-1(H)+/donor-negative mismatch, both ungenotyped) means the ceiling may not exist for this patient at all.

Every response behind rezatapopt is in solid tumors: PYNNACLE ORR 20% (PMID 41740031), all responders KRAS wild-type, zero myeloid patients. The bet stacks two unproven contingencies before you even reach the drug, confirm a TP53 aberration at all off a 2019-mutant-versus-2026-negative discrepancy, then confirm it is specifically Y220C, then supply the venetoclax partner the preclinical biology demands in a patient already refractory to a venetoclax regimen. The myeloid trial NCT06616636 has posted nothing, so there is no clinical read to anchor to.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for post-transplant relapse
comment: No argument that HCT2 is the backbone, but the headline 37% is the related-donor subgroup of a 179-patient retrospective registry (PMID 23918951, ROBINS-I Serious); the pooled cohort sits at 25%. Who reaches a second transplant is selected on fitness and disease control, so the subgroup number flatters the modality. The same analysis names active high-burden disease at HCT2, which is this patient at 85% blasts, as the dominant adverse survival driver.

This is the one tier-1b anchor in the dossier and conservative is right to lean on it: SIERRA (PMID 39298738) is the only randomized phase 3 and it hit its registered dCR endpoint, 17.1% vs 0%, p<0.0001. My one correction to the framing, reading the null ITT OS (HR 0.99, p=0.96) as a pure crossover artifact is plausible but not proven, and dCR stays a surrogate. On evidence tier this is the best-supported pick anyone put forward.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
comment: Concensusite leans on NCCN category 2A for HCT2, but 2A is expert consensus, not RCT-grade evidence, and the number under it is still the confounded related-donor subgroup of a retrospective registry (PMID 23918951, ROBINS-I Serious). The guideline endorsement reflects the absence of anything better in relapsed post-transplant AML rather than a positive randomized result. I don't dispute the rank, only the weight the 2A label is being asked to carry.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after second allo-HCT (Bleakley platform; TSC-100/TSC-101, ALLOHA)
comment: Honoring the patient's stated preference explains the ranking, but preference doesn't upgrade evidence, and this is still n=9, single-arm, feasibility (PMID 38683966), placed above options with an actual phase-3 or on-label read. The eligibility it rides on is entirely biomarker-unconfirmed: HLA-A*02:01, HA-1(H)+/donor-negative genotyping on patient and sibling, and recipient-origin relapse by sorted-CD34 STR chimerism, none of it back. I would fund that workup at rank 1; I would not call the therapy rank 1 until the typing resolves.

The 100% RFS at 44 months advocate cites (PMID 31235963) comes from 12 patients given the product as post-HCT prophylaxis against relapse, not salvage of active disease, which is what an 85%-blast marrow needs. The 54% comparator is a concurrent non-randomized cohort, so the survival contrast is confounded by selection, ROBINS-I Serious. Using MRD/prophylaxis data to rank a lever for florid relapse is a disease-state mismatch, on top of the A*02:01 gate still being open.

No AML guideline carries a p53 reactivator: rezatapopt's only clinical readout is solid-tumor (PYNNACLE, pmid:41740031), the myeloid study nct:NCT06616636 has posted nothing, and it appears in neither NCCN AML v4.2026 nor ELN 2022. Stacking a double biomarker contingency (TP53 aberrant, then Y220C) on a regimen with no consensus category puts this well outside guideline-endorsed use. If the typing lands, the guideline-aligned move is the trial slot, not the drug as off-protocol salvage.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for post-transplant relapse
comment: This is the pick that matches consensus most cleanly: ELN 2022 places a second allo-HCT at the center of curative-intent relapse management once the marrow is back in remission, and NCCN AML v4.2026 keeps it a category 2A option for fit patients. Conservative gets the sequencing right too, conditioning HCT2 on cytoreduction first rather than trying to transplant an 85%-blast marrow. My one add is that ELN treats the cytoreduction step as load-bearing, not a formality, so the real go/no-go rests on the bridge actually working (pmid:23918951).

Critic reads the Sievers single-arm CR+CRp data (pmid:11432892) as thin and lands it near the bottom, but this is the one on-label, guideline-listed agent in the whole slate: NCCN AML v4.2026 carries single-agent gemtuzumab at category 2A for CD33-positive relapsed AML. A 2A rating is the panel's own calibration of exactly the evidence critic is marking down, plus twenty-plus years of post-marketing safety, so 'low evidence' undersells the consensus sitting behind it. Fair to hold it as a cytoreductive bridge rather than definitive therapy, and the pending quantitative CD33 density is the right gate.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T (Bleakley platform; TSC-100/TSC-101, ALLOHA)
comment: On guideline-fit I'm closer to advocate than the rank order suggests: ELN 2022 and NCCN AML v4.2026 both make trial enrollment the preferred R/R route, so HA-1 TCR-T (nct:NCT05473910, pmid:38683966) is guideline-consistent as an enrollment target. The qualifier is that the support is for getting on a trial, not for TCR-T as a modality with any consensus category of its own. Ranking it first also understates that eligibility is still ungenotyped (HLA-A*02:01 plus the HA-1 recipient-positive / donor-negative mismatch), so today she is an enrolling candidate, not a confirmed-eligible one.

target_intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge
comment: For cytoreduction I'd steer to the on-label lever: pivekimab is investigational, not FDA-approved, and shows up in neither NCCN AML v4.2026 nor ELN 2022, whereas gemtuzumab does the same debulk-before-HCT2 job on-label at category 2A. The single-agent number is modest (ORR 21%, pmid:38423051) and the VOD signal cuts against it with a transplant planned. If a CD123 route is wanted it belongs on a trial, not as off-guideline salvage ahead of an approved CD33 ADC.

Putting the HA-1 handle at rank 1 is exactly what this run was submitted for: the file names HLA-restricted immunotherapy as the explicit reason, and the risktaker ranked it where the patient's priority actually sits. The 4-of-9 CR with no DLTs (pmid:38683966) plus a trial the patient will travel for (NCT05473910) satisfies prefers_trials and the curative goal without tripping a veto, since none are on file. My one add: the rank hangs on typing that is fast and cheap to pull, so the plan should read as genotype-the-pair-now, not wait-and-see.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for post-transplant relapse
comment: No argument that HCT2 is the curative backbone the cells have to ride on, and the conservative's insistence on documenting cardiac and organ-function fitness before choosing conditioning intensity genuinely serves the patient here; the preferences file flags that same gap and asks for the 0.75 efficacy weight to be revisited once fitness is known. Where I push back is sequencing: the HLA-A*02:01 typing and HA-1/HA-2 genotyping are fast and cheap, so they should run in parallel with the cytoreduction plan rather than queue behind the transplant, because they are what move the stated-reason axis from undetermined to eligible.

The conservative ranked none of the HLA-restricted axis and said so plainly, but that axis is the documented reason the case came to Libby, so parking it entirely answers a different question than the one the patient asked. I take the point that a phase-1 product with an unretrievable per-grade toxicity table should not outrank an approved agent in a fitness-unknown patient; the honest fix is to tee up the genotyping that resolves eligibility, not to drop the option off the slate. Leaving it unranked without surfacing the cheap workup that unlocks it under-serves the free_text priority.

Ranking the handle the case was built around dead last is defensible on evidence maturity, n=9, single-arm, feasibility rather than efficacy (pmid:38683966), and I will not pretend the 4/9 is more than a signal. But the patient explicitly accepts trials including travel and named this axis as the reason for the run, so a rank driven purely by evidence grade under-weights the preference set I am here to carry. The gating uncertainty is HLA/HA typing and sorted-CD34 STR chimerism, all fast and cheap, which argues for de-risking eligibility now rather than burying the option below gemtuzumab.

Good to see the HA-1 handle at rank 2 and read through the guideline's enroll-in-a-trial language; that is far closer to the patient's stated priority than parking it, and it respects prefers_trials. My caveat is that the guideline endorsement is for trial enrollment generically, whereas this specific mismatched-minor-antigen product (NCT05473910) is the named reason for the run, so it deserves to be teed up as the concrete next step rather than a category placeholder. Eligibility is one genotyping panel away, and that is what should set its position.

Ranking the SIERRA platform last because NCCN/ELN have not yet adopted CD45 radioimmunotherapy inverts the patient's stated preferences: the file explicitly accepts trials including travel and vetoes no modality, so guideline-adoption status is close to the one axis the patient waived. This is the strongest evidence in the dossier for carrying an 85%-blast marrow into the transplant the whole cellular plan depends on, durable CR 22% versus 0% (pmid:39298738), so demoting it below DLI on consensus-fit works against the curative goal. An efficacy lean at 0.75 argues for the enabler, not against it.
